findings.message: The offset is wrong. With `-n 120`, `_offset` is 120 and the first line prints `NR + offset` = 121, not 120, which defeats the stated purpose (`sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120`). The default case only works because `_start` is empty and the offset becomes 0. Use `NR + start - 1`, with the default start set to 1. For example, set `_start=1` initially and pass `offset=$((_start - 1))`.

`lk_check_files number $@` lost its quotes (the original was `"$@"`). File names containing spaces or glob characters are word-split and expanded, so valid files are rejected or the wrong files are checked. Restore `"$@"`.

No tests were added for `-n` in tests/t_number.sh. Cases for the first line number, `-n 1`, `-n 0`, invalid values such as `-n abc`, `-n -1` and `-n ''`, and numbering that continues across multiple files would have caught the off-by-one error.
Very large START values pass the digit check but are passed to awk as doubles and printed with `%d`. They lose precision or overflow, and nothing validates the range.

pull_request.title: number: add -n START to begin numbering at START
pull_request.body:
Adds `-n START` to `linekit number`, so a numbered excerpt can keep the line numbers of the file it was cut from:

    sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120

The command table in README.md is updated.
